rv.q: Hans Litten: The Jew Who Cross-Examined Hitler is a searing dramatization of a long-ago hero’s bleak fate which grimly relates to the present.
The factual subject matter of this play rises above everything in its prescience of what is happening right now in this country.
Grandiosity in service of nothing amounts to a play with few, if any, redeeming qualities.

His story is a compelling source for this play by Douglas Lackey, because Litten stands out as someone who was deeply human in a time forever earmarked in history as a time when the world sat back and lost their humanity in the face of great cruelty and mass murder.

cn.t: Critics find this historical drama about a lawyer who cross-examined Hitler dramatically uneven with clumsy staging and sluggish pacing, but praise its timely, resonant subject matter and philosophical ideas that powerfully echo today's political climate.
